candidates.title: Customer-facing web app returning 5xx errors
candidates.text:
# Customer-facing web app returning 5xx errors

## Symptoms
A customer-facing application returns 500/502/503 errors, or synthetic monitors fail.

## Cause
A bad deployment, exhausted connection pools, autoscaling limits, or failing downstream dependencies.

## Resolution
1. Check the deployment history. If a release happened within the last 24 hours, consider rolling back first.
2. Review application logs and APM traces for the failing endpoint.
3. Check instance counts against autoscaling limits, and check database connection pool metrics.
4. Post customer communication through the status page if the outage lasts more than 15 minutes.

candidates.title: Common how-to requests: self-service index
candidates.text:
# Common how-to requests: self-service index

## Symptoms
User asks how to do a common task such as out-of-office, mapping drives, sharing calendars, or phone email setup.

## Cause
Self-service articles exist but are hard to find.

## Resolution
1. Search the service portal knowledge base with the user's own wording.
2. Send the article link and walk through it if needed.
3. If no article exists, create a knowledge feedback task so one gets written.

candidates.title: Handling a site-wide network outage
candidates.text:
# Handling a site-wide network outage

## Symptoms
Many users at one site report no connectivity at the same time: no internal apps, no internet, and often no desk phones.

## Cause
Core switch failure, upstream carrier circuit outage, or power issue in the main distribution frame.

## Resolution
1. Check the monitoring dashboard for the site's core switch and WAN circuit status.
2. Create a single parent incident and relate every new user report as a child. Do not work each ticket separately.
3. Engage the on-call network engineer and open a carrier ticket if the WAN circuit is down.
4. Post a status update on the service portal banner.
5. After restoration, resolve all child incidents through the parent and open a problem record.

candidates.title: Reporting replica replication lag
candidates.text:
# Reporting replica replication lag

## Symptoms
Reports and dashboards show stale data, or monitoring alerts on replication latency.

## Cause
A stalled log reader or distribution agent, large batch transactions, or IO saturation on the replica.

## Resolution
1. Check replication monitor for latency and agent status.
2. Restart stalled log reader or distribution agents.
3. Check replica disk IO. Pause maintenance jobs if they are saturating IO.
4. Tell reporting users the expected catch-up time.

candidates.title: Report queries timing out on reporting SQL servers
candidates.text:
# Report queries timing out on reporting SQL servers

## Symptoms
A report or dashboard that used to be fast now times out or takes minutes.

## Cause
Query plan regression after a statistics update, or a missing index as tables grow.

## Resolution
1. Identify the query in Query Store or with sp_WhoIsActive while the report runs.
2. Compare current and historical execution plans. If the plan regressed, force the last known good plan.
3. Check for missing index recommendations and table growth.
4. Update statistics and test the report.
5. Create a change request for any new indexes.

candidates.title: SAP performance degradation during month-end close
candidates.text:
# SAP performance degradation during month-end close

## Symptoms
SAP transactions are slow or time out, especially in the last days of the month when finance runs close activities.

## Cause
Month-end batch jobs and heavy reports compete with interactive users for work processes and database resources.

## Resolution
1. Check SM50/SM66 for long-running work processes and SM37 for active batch jobs.
2. Reschedule non-critical batch jobs outside business hours.
3. Temporarily increase dialog work processes using operation modes.
4. Identify custom reports that lock tables and move them to background execution.
5. Engage the DBA team if database wait times are high.

candidates.title: Common SAP invoice posting errors (MIRO)
candidates.text:
# Common SAP invoice posting errors (MIRO)

## Symptoms
Vendor invoice cannot be posted in MIRO or is blocked for payment.

## Cause
Posting period closed, price/quantity variance beyond tolerance, or goods receipt/invoice receipt mismatch.

## Resolution
1. 'Posting period not open': confirm with finance, then open the period in OB52.
2. 'Tolerance limit exceeded': confirm the price with the buyer, then release in MRBR.
3. 'GR/IR mismatch': confirm the goods receipt was posted for the invoiced quantity.
4. Document the resolution for audit purposes.

candidates.title: Purchase order stuck in SAP release workflow
candidates.text:
# Purchase order stuck in SAP release workflow

## Symptoms
PO stays 'in release' with no approver action, or the approver never receives the workitem.

## Cause
The approver in the release strategy left or changed roles, or the workflow errored because of missing master data such as a cost center.

## Resolution
1. Check the workflow log (SWIA) for the PO's workitem status.
2. If the workitem is in error, fix the master data issue and restart the workflow.
3. If the approver is invalid, update the release strategy assignment with HR/finance approval.
4. Forward or restart the workitem to the correct approver.

candidates.title: WMS wave fails to release or pick tasks are not generated
candidates.text:
# WMS wave fails to release or pick tasks are not generated

## Symptoms
Wave release fails or hangs, and no pick tasks are created for the floor.

## Cause
Items with missing master data (dimensions/weight), a stuck SAP-to-WMS order interface, or allocation failures from inventory mismatches.

## Resolution
1. Check the wave's error log in WMS for the failing order or item.
2. Fix missing item master data and re-release the wave.
3. Check the SAP-to-WMS integration queue depth. Restart the listener if it is stuck.
4. Engage the ERP team if orders are not being sent from SAP.

candidates.title: USB-C dock or external monitor issues
candidates.text:
# USB-C dock or external monitor issues

## Symptoms
External monitors are blank or keyboard/mouse on the dock do not work, while the laptop works on its own.

## Cause
Outdated dock firmware or Thunderbolt drivers, a failing dock power supply, or a bad cable.

## Resolution
1. Power-cycle the dock by unplugging its power for 30 seconds.
2. Update dock firmware and the laptop's Thunderbolt/USB-C drivers from the software center.
3. Swap the display cable and test each monitor individually.
4. Replace the dock if the issue persists.

candidates.title: Laptop does not boot or shows BitLocker recovery
candidates.text:
# Laptop does not boot or shows BitLocker recovery

## Symptoms
Laptop does not power on, blue-screens during boot, or prompts for a BitLocker recovery key.

## Cause
BitLocker recovery is usually triggered by BIOS/firmware updates or hardware changes, including motherboard failure. Boot loops are often caused by a failed Windows update; no power or failed diagnostics usually mean a hardware failure.

## Resolution
1. For BitLocker prompts: verify identity, retrieve the recovery key from the device record, and read it to the user.
2. After unlocking, suspend and resume BitLocker.
3. For boot loops: boot to the recovery environment and uninstall the latest quality update.
4. For no power: try a known-good charger and a battery reset.
5. Run vendor diagnostics to check for hardware failure, such as a failed motherboard.
6. If hardware has failed, provide a loaner and open a vendor warranty case.
7. Restore the user's data to the loaner from OneDrive.

candidates.text:
# Lost or stolen company device

## Symptoms
User reports a lost or stolen laptop or phone.

## Cause
N/A. This is a security response procedure.

## Resolution
1. Record where and when the device was lost and whether a police report was filed.
2. Issue a remote lock/wipe through MDM and disable the device object in the directory.
3. Revoke all user sessions and reset the password.
4. Confirm BitLocker was enabled on the device (for compliance reporting).
5. Order a replacement device through End User Computing.

candidates.title: Laptop performance troubleshooting
candidates.text:
# Laptop performance troubleshooting

## Symptoms
Laptop is slow, freezes, boots slowly, or runs the fan constantly.

## Cause
Common causes: low disk space (often OneDrive cache), insufficient RAM for the workload, a stuck security agent scan, or an aging device.

## Resolution
1. Check free disk space. If below 10%, enable OneDrive Files On-Demand and clear temp files.
2. Check Task Manager for processes with high CPU/RAM. Update the endpoint security agent if its scan is stuck.
3. Check device age and RAM. Devices older than 4 years or with 8 GB RAM qualify for refresh.
4. Run hardware diagnostics if freezes continue.

candidates.title: Laptop performance troubleshooting
candidates.text:
# Laptop performance troubleshooting

## Symptoms
Laptop is slow, freezes, boots slowly, or runs the fan constantly.

## Cause
Common causes: low disk space (often OneDrive cache), insufficient RAM for the workload, a stuck security agent scan, or an aging device.

## Resolution
1. Check free disk space. If below 10%, enable OneDrive Files On-Demand and clear temp files.
2. Check Task Manager for processes with high CPU/RAM. Update the endpoint security agent if its scan is stuck.
3. Check device age and RAM. Devices older than 4 years or with 8 GB RAM qualify for refresh.
4. Run hardware diagnostics if freezes continue.

candidates.title: Laptop does not boot or shows BitLocker recovery
candidates.text:
# Laptop does not boot or shows BitLocker recovery

## Symptoms
Laptop does not power on, blue-screens during boot, or prompts for a BitLocker recovery key.

## Cause
BitLocker recovery is usually triggered by BIOS/firmware updates or hardware changes, including motherboard failure. Boot loops are often caused by a failed Windows update; no power or failed diagnostics usually mean a hardware failure.

## Resolution
1. For BitLocker prompts: verify identity, retrieve the recovery key from the device record, and read it to the user.
2. After unlocking, suspend and resume BitLocker.
3. For boot loops: boot to the recovery environment and uninstall the latest quality update.
4. For no power: try a known-good charger and a battery reset.
5. Run vendor diagnostics to check for hardware failure, such as a failed motherboard.
6. If hardware has failed, provide a loaner and open a vendor warranty case.
7. Restore the user's data to the loaner from OneDrive.

candidates.title: SAP performance degradation during month-end close
candidates.text:
# SAP performance degradation during month-end close

## Symptoms
SAP transactions are slow or time out, especially in the last days of the month when finance runs close activities.

## Cause
Month-end batch jobs and heavy reports compete with interactive users for work processes and database resources.

## Resolution
1. Check SM50/SM66 for long-running work processes and SM37 for active batch jobs.
2. Reschedule non-critical batch jobs outside business hours.
3. Temporarily increase dialog work processes using operation modes.
4. Identify custom reports that lock tables and move them to background execution.
5. Engage the DBA team if database wait times are high.

candidates.title: Mobile email and MDM compliance issues
candidates.text:
# Mobile email and MDM compliance issues

## Symptoms
Outlook mobile stops syncing, reports non-compliance, or loops on sign-in. MDM enrollment fails.

## Cause
Outdated OS version below the compliance policy, device enrollment limit reached, or stale device records.

## Resolution
1. Check the device's compliance status and reason in MDM.
2. Have the user update the phone OS to the minimum supported version.
3. Remove stale device records if the user is at the enrollment limit.
4. Have the user run 'Check status' in Company Portal, then reopen Outlook.

candidates.title: Re-registering MFA after a phone replacement
candidates.text:
# Re-registering MFA after a phone replacement

## Symptoms
User cannot complete MFA because the Authenticator app was lost or not transferred to a new device.

## Cause
Authenticator registrations are bound to the original device and are not always restored from phone backups.

## Resolution
1. Verify identity using a manager callback. Do not rely on information the caller provides alone.
2. In the identity portal, revoke existing MFA sessions and delete the old Authenticator registration.
3. Issue a Temporary Access Pass valid for 1 hour.
4. Guide the user through registering the Authenticator app at the security info page.
5. Confirm a successful sign-in before resolving.

candidates.title: Troubleshooting SSO failures for SaaS applications
candidates.text:
# Troubleshooting SSO failures for SaaS applications

## Symptoms
User gets redirect loops, 'user not assigned', or SAML errors when opening a SaaS app from the SSO portal.

## Cause
Common causes: the app assignment was removed after an HR department change, the user's email/UPN attribute does not match the app, or a stale browser session.

## Resolution
1. Check the user's app assignments in the IdP admin console.
2. If the assignment is missing, re-add the user to the app's access group (department changes can remove it).
3. Compare the user's UPN/email in the IdP with the username in the target app.
4. Have the user clear cookies or try an InPrivate window.
5. Escalate to the application team only if the IdP shows a successful SAML assertion.
